page: Amazon Web Services t3.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose virtual machine running on the AWS Nitro system. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, the instance exposes 4 vCPUs across 2 physical execution cores via simultaneous multithreading. Memory provisioning includes 16.0 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The configuration contains no onboard local storage, relying on network-attached storage architectures, and features no dedicated GPU hardware. Network interfaces deliver a baseline throughput of 1 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are assigned.

Benchmark evaluations position the t3.xlarge predominantly in the lower quartiles of compute and throughput capabilities due to its shared burstable architecture. Stress-ng assessments yielded 1140.79 points in single-core and 3253.57 points in multi-core metrics, both falling into the bottom 25 percent. In Geekbench testing, the server attained 946.0 points in single-core and 2125.0 points in multi-core operations. Memory subsystems achieved 23.93 GB/sec in uncached read bandwidth and 20.41 GB/sec in uncached write throughput. High-throughput tasks also registered lower-tier performance, with static web serving measured at 2.74 GB/sec and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression at 10.77 GB/sec.

The primary operational tradeoff of the t3.xlarge is its reliance on CPU credits, making continuous high-utilization compute runs sub-optimal once burst capacity is depleted. Consequently, cost efficiency is realized when executing sporadic, low-duty-cycle tasks that utilize its generous 16 GB memory footprint without saturating CPU threads. The instance is suited for staging environments, development servers, internal web serving, low-traffic microservices, and modest caching or lightweight background data processing.
description: Amazon Web Services t3.xlarge is a burstable general-purpose virtual instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor platform. It features an Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processor operating at 2.5 GHz with 4 vCPUs across 2 physical cores, accompanied by 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory at a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The configuration includes no integrated local storage or dedicated graphics hardware, operating with a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. In benchmark evaluations, the t3.xlarge demonstrates baseline-tier performance, recording a Geekbench multi-core score of 2125.0 and stress-ng multi-core score of 3253.57, aligning with its burstable credit-governed profile. The instance provides cost-effective resource utilization for applications that require moderate memory allocations without demanding continuous peak CPU execution, making it appropriate for development environments, low-traffic web applications, microservices, and small-scale caching layers.
